SOURCE = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

Clique.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}

    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a clique of AT LEAST k vertices: k vertices with an
edge between every two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
always no.

WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-w8y_00dv

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Clique.

Reduction
---------
Given a Vertex Cover instance (G, k) with n vertices, build the complement
graph G' on the same vertex set 0..n-1, whose edges are exactly the pairs
that are NOT edges of G.  Return the Clique instance (G', n - k).

Correctness
-----------
A set S of vertices is a vertex cover of G (every edge of G has an endpoint
in S) iff its complement V \\ S is an independent set of G (no edge of G has
both endpoints outside S).  An independent set of G is exactly a clique of
the complement graph G'.  Therefore:

    G has a vertex cover of size <= k
    <=> G has an independent set of size >= n - k
    <=> G' has a clique of size >= n - k.

So the source answer is yes iff the target answer is yes.

Edge cases line up with the documented ones:
  * k < 0  -> target k' = n - k > n, and Clique is no for k' > n.
  * k >= n -> target k' = n - k <= 0, and Clique is yes for k' <= 0.
  * no edges -> G' is complete, which has a clique of size n, so the target
    is yes exactly when n - k <= n, i.e. k >= 0.
  * n = 0  -> G' has no vertices; target yes iff k' <= 0 iff k >= 0.

The construction runs in O(n^2) time, which is polynomial in the encoding
length of the instance.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import combinations
from typing import Any

Instance = dict[str, Any]


def reduce(instance: Instance) -> Instance:
    """Reduce a Vertex Cover instance to an equivalent Clique instance."""
    n = instance["n"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # Set of undirected edges of the source graph, orientation-independent.
    source_edges = {frozenset(edge) for edge in instance["edges"]}

    # Complement graph: keep every pair that is not a source edge.
    complement_edges = [
        [u, v]
        for u, v in combinations(range(n), 2)
        if frozenset((u, v)) not in source_edges
    ]

    return {"n": n, "edges": complement_edges, "k": n - k}
EOF

"""Tests comparing Vertex Cover brute force with the reduction to Clique."""

import random

from problems import SOURCE, TARGET
from reduce import reduce


def check(instance):
    reduced = reduce(instance)
    # The reduction must produce a valid target instance.
    TARGET.validate(reduced)
    expected = SOURCE.is_yes(instance)
    got = TARGET.is_yes(reduced)
    assert got == expected, (
        f"mismatch for {instance}: source={expected}, "
        f"reduced={reduced}, target={got}"
    )
    return reduced


def main():
    tests_run = 0

    # Exhaustive small instances: all graphs up to 4 vertices with all k.
    for scale in range(0, 5):
        for instance in SOURCE.enumerate_instances(scale):
            n = instance["n"]
            for k in range(-2, n + 3):
